summary:
MOONSHIFT is a browser game that turns real NASA space-weather data into a lunar mission for kids aged 7–12. Players run a Moon base through 30 real days (17 April – 16 May 2024) from NASA’s DONKI database. That month brought X-class solar flares, including an X8.7, and the strongest geomagnetic storm in over 20 years (10 May 2024).
Each day is a short level. When a flare knocks out the radio, the player tunes the antenna back to Earth; when a solar particle storm hits, they race the crew into the shelter. Calm days bring station chores as mini-games: harvesting the greenhouse, wiping Moon dust off solar panels, building a shield wall from regolith or water tanks. Every level ends with a simple space fact. Every button shows exactly what changes (radiation, food and air, energy, mood, science), so children learn cause and effect instead of guessing. It runs in any browser, in Ukrainian and English, with no
accounts or tracking. As NASA’s Artemis missions return people to the Moon, space weather becomes a real hazard. Our trainer helps children understand it and practise calm, careful decisions. https://github.com/AnnaYal5/Moonshift_junior_trainer.git
details:
What it does and how it works
MoonShift is a browser game for kids aged 7–12. The player runs a lunar base for 30 days, and each day is built from real space weather recorded between 17 April and 16 May 2024 in NASA's DONKI database, including the huge solar storm of 10 May 2024. On calm days the player picks a base job and plays a short mini-game. On storm days they must choose quickly between hiding in the shelter and working on while taking more radiation. Every choice changes five meters: battery, life support, mood, radiation dose and science. Each option shows its cost before the player picks it. The game ends with a launch home and a Junior Astronaut certificate.

Benefits and impact
Kids experience the real trade-offs mission planners face, like power vs. safety and science vs. radiation. They also learn that space weather is real, can be forecast, and that radiation dose never goes down.

Tools
JavaScript, React 19, Vite and CSS. Node.js scripts download the DONKI data, turn it into 30 game days, and simulate many playthroughs to balance the game. It's deployed with Docker and nginx. No special hardware was needed.

Creativity
The real Sun designs the levels. Players get CME warnings days in advance, like real forecasters, and the lunar night falls on the same dates as on the real Moon. Base jobs become mini-games such as Panel Patrol and Brick Builder.

Factors we considered
Plain language, a no-timer mode for younger kids, no free choices, a retry option instead of game over, Ukrainian and English versions, no download or account, and honest credit for the NASA data.
